interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / computistic diagram of the year, the seasons and their qualities (a scheme of interlocking circles)
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram shows the year ("ANNVS", written in the centre) as a ring of overlapping arcs or lenses, each holding the name of a season and the qualities attached to it. Reading the labels: "uer" (ver, spring) is paired with "humidus" and "calidus" (moist and hot). "eſtas" (summer) is paired with "calidus" and "ſiccus" (hot and dry). "autumnus" is paired with "ſiccus" and "frigidus" (dry and cold). "hiems" (winter) is paired with "frigidus" and "humidus" (cold and moist). Each season therefore lies in the overlap of two adjacent qualities, and each quality is shared by two neighbouring seasons. This matches the medieval scheme in which the four seasons correspond to pairs of the four qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry). The Step 1 fragments "o ri eng", "me ri dies", "oc ci dens" and "sep ten [tr]io" can be read as the cardinal directions: oriens (east) with spring, meridies (south) with summer, occidens (west) with autumn, and septentrio (north) with winter. The diagram thus links year, seasons, qualities and directions, presumably the four elements and humours as well, although these are not named in the diagram. The qualities are placed in a cyclical order: humid and hot (spring), hot and dry (summer), dry and cold (autumn), cold and moist (winter). The arcs are coloured in yellow, brown-red and green, and the outer ring encloses the whole scheme as a unified year.
interpretation.evidence: The transcribed labels "uer", "eſtas", "autum nus" and "hiems" are season names (spring, summer, autumn, winter) written in Latin, while "humidus", "calidus", "ſiccus" and "frigidus" are the standard Latin names of the qualities. The central "ANNVS" identifies the whole as the year. The fragments "o ri eng", "me ri dies", "oc ci dens" and "sep ten" match the syllables of oriens, meridies, occidens and septentrio, but they are split over several lines and some are hard to read; Step 1 entry 10 (illegible text near "sep ten") is probably the final syllable "trio", and the reading of entry 22 ("oc ci dens") is uncertain, so these directional readings are less secure. The Step 1 relations that use "connected_to" for bands separating areas are approximate, since the bands act as arc boundaries that overlap rather than as true connections. Step 1 is also missing a separate entry for the individual overlapping arcs. The pairing of seasons with qualities relies on the standard medieval tradition of such diagrams; no specific source is named because I am not certain of the exact text.
